newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Tsumeb concludes 10.5 pct wage increase.
newsitem.headline: Tsumeb concludes 10.5 pct wage increase.

text.p: Tsumeb Corp Ltd in Namibia and the Mineworkers Union of Nambia (MUN) have agreed on a 10.5 percent wage increase, owners Gold Fields of Namibia Ltd said on Monday.
The agreement, reached on Saturday, ends a bitter six-week old strike which exploded into crisis last week after MUN members took control of the group's three mines -- Otjihase, Kombat and Tsumeb.
"Yes, this means the strike is now over. It officially ended at midnight on Saturday," a Tsumeb spokesman told Reuters.
Substantial agreement was also reached on a retrenchment package for employees who would no longer be employed by TCL.
The company said terms and conditions of employment and retrenchment would be discussed with the other categories of workers "immediately".
Gold Fields said that the Otjihase Mine was flooding and water from the old mine at Tsumeb, which supplies the town, is threatened with contamination.
Tsumeb mines and smelters, owned by Goldfields of Namibia, have been shut down since August 23. The company anticipates that it will have full and free access to all operations shortly.
The strike cost TCL some 80 tonnes a day in lost copper production and a similar amount in lost lead.
